title: Accuracy, readability, and quality of websites about metastatic renal cell carcinoma treatment
screen_reason: Cross-sectional analysis of 39 patient-facing websites about metastatic renal cell carcinoma treatment, selected from 2,700 search-engine queries. One domain of the analysis is 'correctness': a medical oncologist read every website and identified statements inconsistent with the NCCN Kidney Cancer v4.2023 guidelines. The paper reports the share of websites carrying at least one incorrect statement (12/39, 31%), which is a CONTENT prevalence estimate with an explicit external ground truth. The completeness, readability, QUEST and DISCERN results are quality/readability measures and are not extracted as prevalence.

estimates.country: Not stated; English-language websites retrieved from US-based searches, publishers include US, Canadian, UK and Australian organisations
estimates.platform: Google, Yahoo and Bing search results (patient-facing websites)
estimates.measure_type: % of eligible patient-facing mRCC treatment websites containing at least one statement incorrect against NCCN guidelines
estimates.value_raw: Twelve (31%) websites had >=1 incorrect statement (12/39); 68 incorrect statements in total, median 1, range 0-8 per website
estimates.denominator: 39 eligible English-language patient-facing websites about mRCC treatment, selected from the first 25 links of 36 keyword permutations across Google, Yahoo and Bing (2,700 queries)
estimates.definition: Website contained at least one statement judged inconsistent with the National Comprehensive Cancer Network - Kidney Cancer Version 4.2023 guidelines, for example listing homeopathy or hormone therapy as an mRCC treatment option, or carrying outdated statements
estimates.misinfo_def: Correctness by identifying incorrect statements that were inconsistent with guidelines
estimates.source_quote: Twelve (31%) websites had ≥1 incorrect statement, such as listing homeopathy or hormone therapy as mRCC treatment options, or including outdated statements.
estimates.page_loc: Abstract, Results; also section 3.3 Accuracy-correctness, p. 375.e3-375.e7
estimates.ground_truth_detail: One medical oncologist (DHK) reviewed all websites against NCCN Kidney Cancer v4.2023; statements that were not clearly incorrect were discussed with a second medical oncologist (AD or KF). No reliability coefficient is reported for the correctness domain (Cronbach's alpha was computed for completeness and DISCERN only).

estimates.notes: Denominator is the website, not the statement: a site with 8 incorrect statements counts once. Rank-truncated search sets (first 25 links per query) make the frame curated. The 68 incorrect statements have no denominator of statements, so no statement-level row is possible.

missed_or_uncertain: Not extracted, all quality/readability rather than veracity: (a) mean completeness score 30% (9.6 of 32 checklist items) and 'only 2 (5%) websites had a passing score' of >=60% - completeness against an NCI-derived checklist measures omission, not falsity, so a wholly accurate but brief site fails it; I judged this QUALITY-side and left it out rather than carrying it as a CONTENT row; (b) DISCERN categories (7 (18%) excellent, 22 (56%) good, 10 (26%) fair) and mean QUEST 19/28 - quality instruments; unlike the prostate-cancer paper in this batch there is no single composite 'low quality' share to carry, so no QUALITY row was created; (c) readability grades (Fry 11th, SMOG 12th, no site below 9th grade) - not a share of misinformation. The count of 68 incorrect statements across 13 categories has no statement-level denominator and so cannot become a row.

rob.design: Cross-sectional website analysis. 2,700 queries (36 keyword permutations x first 25 links x Google/Yahoo/Bing) in cleared incognito Chrome, 23-26 May 2023, yielding 39 eligible English-language patient-facing websites after excluding sponsored, video-primary, social media, provider-facing, pharmaceutical, news, duplicate and paediatric sites. Completeness scored by 2 independent raters against a 32-item checklist derived from the NCI PDQ patient version and refined by 3 mRCC oncologists, with Cronbach's alpha reported for inter-rater reliability; correctness judged by a single oncologist against NCCN v4.2023 with a second oncologist consulted on unclear statements; QUEST scored by one author; DISCERN by two independent scorers. Discrepant scores were discussed but raters could keep their own score, so 'consensus' is partial.
